s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive orbital and facial syndrome with mass effect
key_facts: History of nodular sclerosing type stage IIE Hodgkin lymphoma
Treated with 4 cycles of ABVC and 3060 cGY radiation
Previous excisions of left upper eyelid mass
Multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells on histopathology
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and negative for CD45, S100, desmin, and lysozyme
MRI shows lesion with marked interval enlargement within the orbit and extension through the frontal sinus into the intracranial compartment
Tumor centered at the left cavernous sinus and orbital apex involving the left intracavernous/supraclinoid segments of the internal carotid artery
Extension into the right cavernous sinus and right sphenoid sinus with mass effect on the left temporal lobe
Genetic testing shows splicing variant (c.2515-1G>A) in the PALB2 gene

raw.rationale: The patient's history of Hodgkin lymphoma and the presence of a multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells on histopathology, along with the tumor's aggressive behavior and extension into the orbit and intracranial compartment, are consistent with orbital lymphoma, particularly given the patient's previous cancer diagnosis.

rejected.label: solitary fibrous tumor of the lacrimal gland
rejected.why: The histopathology and imaging findings do not support this diagnosis, as solitary fibrous tumors typically have a more benign appearance and do not usually exhibit such aggressive behavior.

rejected.label: sarcoidosis
rejected.why: The histopathology does not show non-caseating granulomas, which are characteristic of sarcoidosis, and the patient's history and imaging findings are not consistent with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: orbital lymphangioma
rejected.why: The histopathology and imaging findings do not support this diagnosis, as orbital lymphangiomas typically have a more cystic appearance and do not usually exhibit such aggressive behavior.

rejected.label: metastases
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of cancer, the histopathology and genetic testing results suggest a primary orbital lymphoma rather than metastatic disease from the previous Hodgkin lymphoma.
